title: Repeated Note

illustrates.quote: Include both page location information and reference marks, when given. Note: Do not repeat a referenced note in a volume of endnotes, where notes are transcribed exactly as written. (See Sample 16-6: Repeated Note on page 16-23.)

blocks.text: … Do you feel that it is acceptable for a counselor to act as an expert in viability—or employment opportunities that could result from a music education[ref:4]?
blocks.features: First print page, ending with a superscript numeral-4 reference mark; print page number '72' boxed at the top right.

blocks.text: [ref:4] See: A Blind Music Student's College Survival Guide
blocks.features: Footnote at the foot of print page 72.

blocks.text: … And, how many are aware that published labor statistics clearly dispel these myths[ref:5]? …
blocks.features: Second print page (73), ending with a superscript numeral-5 reference mark; print page number '73' boxed at the top right.
Footnote at the foot of print page 73, itself referring back to note 4 on the previous page rather than repeating its full text in print.

notes.text: See: A Blind Music Student's College Survival Guide

print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 16.7.5, illustrating a note ('See note 4') that refers to an earlier note on a different print page; per the rule, the referenced note (4) is repeated in braille after the original note (5), rather than left as a bare page-turn-back reference.
print.printFeatures: Two boxed print pages (72 and 73, separated by a '—New Print Page—' marker), each with a superscript reference mark and its own footnote; the second footnote merely says 'See note 4' in print.

braille.notes: Line-number field width 5 (max line number 17, two digits, +3). Per rule 16.7.5, braille note 5 ('See note #d', i.e. 'See note 4') is followed immediately by a full repetition of note 4's own text ('See: A Blind Music Student's College Survival Guide') -- the referenced note is repeated after the referencing note, in this single braille page, even though print left it as a bare cross-reference. A single print-page-change indicator (#gb) appears at the very start (right-flush on line 1), and a second one (#gc) after note 4's first occurrence, marking the two print pages combined onto one braille page.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.5.d per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: lines 13044 and 13052 (field width 5, digits(17)+3) are each exactly 40 characters, the second a dashed page-change rule ending '#gc'. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
